tools.description:
Generates a new screen within a project from a text prompt.

**Instructions for Tool Call:**
*  This action can take a few minutes to complete. Please be patient. DO NOT RETRY.
*  If the tool fails with a timeout, don't retry. Instead, try to get the screen with `get_screen` method every 30 seconds for up to 10 times before giving up.
*  If the tool call fails due to connection error, the generation process may still succeed. Please try to get the screen with `get_screen` method later.

**Output:**
*  **`output_components`**: If `output_components` contains text, return it to the user. If `output_components` contains suggestions (e.g. "Yes, make them all"), present these suggestions to the user. If the user accepts one of the suggestions, call `generate_screen_from_text` again with `prompt` set to the accepted suggestion.

designSystem.description: Optional. The design system id to use for generating the new screen, should always be configured for design consistency, via `get_project` or `list_assets` methods. If not provided, a default design system will be used. Example: `assets/15996705518239280238`.

## Marca
- Claim: "Activa tu potencial" | Hashtag: #PotencialDigital2026
- 3er Congreso Extremeño de Transformación Digital, IA y Ciberseguridad
- Tono: Educativo, Directo, Atrevido, Digital

## Modo visual
- Dark mode nativo (fondo #000000 o #121212)
- Alta saturación, colores vibrantes sobre fondo oscuro
- Estética tecnológica con toques flúor

## Colores
- Primary: #1400C5 (azul eléctrico) — fondos, iconos, brand
- Secondary: #FF4A1F (naranja vivo) — impacto, gradientes, fotografía
- Tertiary: #09EBE1 (cyan) — acentos tecnológicos, detalles
- Accent/CTA: #E1FF2D (amarillo flúor) — botones, highlights, CTAs
- Error: #FF2E63 (rosa neón) — errores, alertas
- Surface: #121212 — cards, modals
- On Surface: #FFFFFF — texto principal

## Tipografía (en app Flutter se usan las fuentes reales)
- Display/Headlines: Lemon (custom, condensada, industrial) → en Stitch: Montserrat Black/ExtraBold
- Body/UI: Darker Grotesque → en Stitch: DM Sans

## Responsive — 3 breakpoints obligatorios
- Mobile: < 600px (1 columna, bottom nav, touch targets 48px)
- Tablet: 600-1024px (2 columnas, rail nav, densidad media)
- Desktop: > 1024px (3+ columnas, side nav, densidad alta, hover states)

## Componentes clave
- Cards con borde sutil (#1E1E1E) sobre fondo #121212
- Botones primarios: fondo #E1FF2D (flúor), texto #000000
- Botones secundarios: borde #1400C5, texto #FFFFFF
- Inputs: fondo #1A1A1A, borde #333333, focus #1400C5
- AppBar: transparente o #000000 con blur
- Bottom Nav: #121212 con iconos #FFFFFF, activo #E1FF2D

## Fotografía
- Personajes IA con iluminación cinematográfica naranja/azul/cyan
- Retratos sobre fondo negro, contraste dramático
- Diversidad de edad y género

## Recursos gráficos
- Patrones geométricos modulares (círculos concéntricos, radiantes)
- Gradientes de barras verticales (naranja-negro, cyan-negro, rosa-azul)
- Tipografía como arte (claim como pieza gráfica)

## Reglas de diseño para pantallas
1. SIEMPRE dark mode — fondo #000000 o #121212
2. El amarillo flúor #E1FF2D es SOLO para CTAs y highlights — no para fondos grandes
3. Máximo 2 colores corporativos dominantes por pantalla + flúor como acento
4. Textos siempre blancos sobre fondo oscuro, nunca grises claros
5. Iconografía: outlined, stroke 1.5-2px, estilo minimal
6. Espaciado generoso (16-24px entre secciones)
7. Cards: bordes redondeados 8px, sin sombra, borde sutil
8. Las imágenes de personajes se usan en onboarding y marketing, NO en UI funcional
9. Los gradientes se usan como fondo de headers/hero, NO en componentes interactivos

SpecBox Control Panel — Design Guidelines

## Brand Identity
- Product: SpecBox Control Panel — internal observability & dev-team management tool over a Postgres Native Backend.
- Aesthetic: Custom, Linear-style (references: Linear, Vercel Dashboard, GitHub Projects, Datadog).
- Visual tone: technical, calm, precise. A daily-use power-user tool, NOT a marketing site.
- Default appearance: LIGHT. (A dark theme exists in code via a toggle; always generate LIGHT here.)

## Color System
- Primary: #0080FF (electric-blue) — CTAs, links, focus rings, active nav item, active claims.
- Secondary: #00B4D8 (cyan-tech) — secondary buttons, tags, the 'done' state.
- Tertiary/Accent: #7C3AED (violet) — highlights, notifications, progress emphasis.
- Neutral seed: #94A3B8 (slate) — borders, dividers, secondary text, disabled.
- Surfaces (light): page bg #F8FAFC (snow), cards #FFFFFF, alt sections #F1F5F9.
- Semantic: Success #10B981, Warning #F59E0B, Error #EF4444, Info #0080FF.
- RULE: Primary buttons = solid #0080FF bg, white text. Secondary buttons = white bg, 1px slate border.
- RULE: Card bg #FFFFFF on a #F8FAFC page. Never use gradients on backgrounds — flat colors only.

## UC Status colors (status semaphore, used sparingly)
- backlog: neutral grey badge (#F1F5F9 bg, #475569 text).
- in_progress: electric-blue badge (#E6F2FF bg, #004C99 text).
- review: amber badge (#FFFBEB bg, #92400E text).
- done: cyan badge (#E0F7FC bg, #006C82 text).

## Typography
- Headings: Sora, semibold/bold, sizes 30/24/20/18px (h1/h2/h3/h4). Page titles are contained (~30px) — this is a tool, not a hero.
- Body: Inter, regular, 16px base, line-height 1.5.
- Labels/captions/buttons: Inter, medium, 14px.
- Monospace (branch names, IDs, code): JetBrains Mono, 13px.
- RULE: max 2 font weights per card.

## Shape & Spacing
- Border radius: 8px base. Buttons 8px, cards 12px, inputs 8px, badges full/pill.
- Spacing: 4px grid. Card padding 16-20px. Section gaps 32px.
- RULE: all interactive elements >= 44px tap target on mobile.

## Layout — Linear-style shell
- Persistent LEFT SIDEBAR, 240px wide, collapsible to a 64px icon rail. Sidebar holds: brand wordmark (◆ SpecBox) + project switcher at top; nav items (Dashboard, Proyectos, Claims, Actividad, Equipo); theme toggle + user at bottom.
- TOP BAR inside the content area: breadcrumb (Proyecto › US-XXX › UC-YYY) on the left, a Cmd+K search trigger and actions on the right. 56-64px tall.
- MAIN content area uses the full width (no narrow centered column) to favor information density.
- A right-side DETAIL PANEL slides in when a table row (e.g. a UC) is selected.

## Component patterns
- Cards: #FFFFFF bg, 12px radius, shadow-sm, 1px border #E2E8F0, 16-20px padding.
- Metric tiles: large number (Sora) + label + small trend arrow + tiny sparkline.
- Data tables: dense, ~38px rows, sticky header with solid bg, left-aligned text, right-aligned numbers, status badge centered. Hover highlights the row. Keyboard navigable.
- Activity feed: vertical timeline, each item = colored dot + actor avatar + action text + relative time.
- Claims: a persistent badge 'avatar @ branch · 23h' using JetBrains Mono for the branch; a dedicated Claims table has a 'duration' column and a 'release' action; stale claims tinted with warning.
- Avatars: initials on a colored circle (rotating electric-blue / cyan / violet by developer).
- Buttons: 8px radius, 14px Inter medium, 12px 24px padding.
- Inputs: 8px radius, 1px #CBD5E1 border, focus ring 2px #0080FF/20%.
- Command palette (Cmd+K): centered overlay modal, search input + grouped results (projects / UCs / developers / actions).
- Empty states: minimal line illustration + one-line explanation + a primary action.
- Skeleton loaders (not spinners) that mirror the final layout.

## Motion (moderate, <200ms, 'calmer interface')
- page enter: fade + 8px slide-up, 180ms ease-out.
- row/button hover: subtle bg change, 120ms.
- panel/modal: scale 0.98->1 + fade, 140ms.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

## Responsive
- Desktop >=1024px: full shell (sidebar 240px + detail panel).
- Tablet 768-1023px: sidebar collapsed to icon rail; detail panel becomes an overlay.
- Mobile <768px: sidebar -> hamburger drawer + a bottom nav of 4 destinations (Dashboard, Proyectos, Claims, Equipo). Dense tables reflow to stacked cards (label:value), surfacing the 2-3 key fields.

## Do NOT
- Do NOT use gradients on backgrounds.
- Do NOT use a top horizontal nav as the primary navigation — the sidebar is primary.
- Do NOT center content in a narrow column — use width for density.
- Do NOT use spinners where a skeleton fits.
- Do NOT exceed shadow-md on cards.
- Do NOT mix sharp and rounded corners in the same mIAsistente Dashboard — Design Instructions

## Product context
Personal single-tenant web dashboard for a Spanish freelance developer (autónomo). Surfaces billing (FacturasApp), email (Gmail+Outlook unified), calendar (Google), and activity (Strava/Garmin — Fase 3 placeholder). Single user. Professional finance tool, NOT consumer fintech.

## Aesthetic: Fintech high-density (Stripe + Mercury)
Dark canónica, light toggle. Mercury bg stack: base #0F0F14 / surface #191920 / elevated #262630. Off-white text #EDEDF3 (NOT pure white).

**References to emulate**: Mercury (sophisticated dark, side panels, Data Views), Stripe (KPI card, Cmd+K, tabular figures), Linear (keyboard-first density), Whoop (single hero metric).
**References to avoid**: Notion softness, Wave SMB-feel, Xero dated, glassmorphism, decorative gradients.

## Color rules
- Accent #5A6BFF used SPARINGLY: primary CTAs, focus rings (2px), active sidebar item, brand wordmark.
- Semantic colors ONLY for status (never decorative):
  - success #34D399 (paid, income)
  - warning #FBBF24 (draft, pending)
  - danger #F87171 (voided, error)
  - info #60A5FA (informational)
- Status pills: bg = soft (12% alpha) + text = full saturation, 11px uppercase, letter-spacing 0.06em.
- NO gradients, NO illustrations, NO glassmorphism in dashboard cards.

## Typography (HARD RULES)
- UI font: Inter (400/500/600/700)
- Mono font: JetBrains Mono (400/500/600)
- ALL monetary amounts use JetBrains Mono with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums`. NO exceptions.
- ALL amounts in tables right-aligned with mono.
- KPI big numbers: 28-36px JetBrains Mono 500, line-height 1.1.
- Labels: 11px Inter 500 uppercase letter-spacing 0.06em color #78788C.
- Body: 14px Inter 400 line-height 1.5.

## Type scale
- xs 11px (labels, status pills)
- sm 13px (table cells, secondary)
- base 14px (body)
- md 16px (emphasis, button)
- lg 20px (card titles)
- xl 28px (KPI big numbers)
- 2xl 36px (hero KPI)
- 3xl 45px (page hero, rare)

## Spacing (Stripe Apps tokens)
0, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 (px)

## Radius
- xs 2px (micro tags)
- sm 4px (status pills, small buttons)
- md 6px (buttons, inputs)
- lg 10px (cards, popovers, dialogs)
- xl 16px (hero cards, modals)
- full 9999px (avatars)

## Layout
- AppShell: Sidebar 240px (collapsible 64px) + Topbar 56px sticky + Main max-w 1440px
- Home: bento grid 12-col (heterogeneous tile sizes — NOT uniform)
  - 6×1 KPI hero "Facturado del mes" + sparkline + dotted predictive
  - 3×1 "Trimestre 303" tile (IVA repercutido / soportado / cuota)
  - 3×1 "Trimestre 130" tile (IRPF a cuenta)
  - 6×2 "Top 5 clientes YTD" with horizontal bars
  - 3×1 "Mini-cal semana" with event dots
  - 3×1 "Emails sin leer" + "Última actividad" stacked

## Tables (Mercury spreadsheet style)
- Row 44px, header 36px
- Padding 12v / 16h
- NO zebra. Only 1px dividers rgba(255,255,255,0.06)
- Sticky header on scroll
- Header text: 11px uppercase letter-spacing 0.06em weight 500 color #78788C
- Click row → side detail panel slides from right (480px)
- Filter chip bar above with removable chips
- Saved Views as sidebar entries (Mercury Data Views pattern)

## Side detail panel
- 480px width, 240ms ease-out slide-in from right
- bg #191920, shadow lg, border-subtle left
- Sticky header + actions, scrollable body
- Close: X icon, Esc, click backdrop

## Empty states
- Icon 48px tertiary centered
- Headline 20px weight 500 POSITIVE ("Conecta Strava o Garmin..." NOT "No hay datos")
- Description 14px secondary
- 1-2 CTAs
- **Ghost cards pattern**: render real card layout at 30% opacity with backdrop-blur 4px below the empty state copy

## Components

### KpiCard
```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ FACTURADO DEL MES               │  11px uppercase tertiary
│                                 │
│ €12.450,00     ↑ 12.4% +€420   │  36px mono / 13px green semantic
│                                 │
│ ╱╲╱╲___╱╲╱   ╴╴╴╴╴╴            │  60px sparkline solid + dotted forecast
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```
bg #191920, radius 10px, border subtle, padding 24px.

### MetricTile (303 / 130)
- Label uppercase top
- Rows of label + amount (right-aligned tabular)
- Divider before total
- Total 18px mono 600
- Ghost button "Generar 303 →" bottom

### DataTable invoice row
Columns: Número | Cliente | Fecha | Estado | Importe
- Número: mono 13px (e.g. 2026/047)
- Cliente: sans 14px 500, truncate
- Fecha: mono 13px (2026-04-27)
- Estado: status pill (emitida=info, pagada=success, borrador=warning, anulada=danger)
- Importe: mono 14px 600, right-aligned, € suffix

### Email row (unified)
Layout: [acct dot 6px] [unread dot] Sender · Subject — preview · Date
- Acct dot color per provider (Gmail red, Outlook blue)
- Unread: bold sender + accent dot

### Activity card (cycling, ghost in v1)
- Hero map/photo 16:9 full-bleed
- 3 big tabular numbers below: Distancia / Tiempo / Vel. media
- Sport color left border 4px (#FC4C02 ride, #2CC36B run)

### Status pill
- Bg semantic-soft (12% alpha) + text semantic full saturation
- 11px / 500 / uppercase / letter-spacing 0.06em
- Padding 2px 8px, radius 4px

### Command palette (Cmd+K)
- Centered 25% top, max-w 560px
- bg #262630, radius 10px, shadow xl
- Sections: Páginas / Facturas / Clientes / Acciones
- Live filter

## Privacy (modo demo) toggle in topbar
When ON, mask:
- Importes: €12.450,00 → €••••••
- NIFs: 12345678A → ***5678*
- Cliente: ACME Corp SL → █████████
- Email: cliente@empresa.com → c••••@•••.com
Transition 180ms ease-out blur. Badge "MODO DEMO" topbar accent-soft bg.

## Iconography
Lucide library, 1.5px stroke ALWAYS. NO filled, NO duotone.
Sizes: 14/16/20/24/48px. Color currentColor.
Key icons: LayoutDashboard, Receipt, Mail, Calendar, Activity, Settings, Search, Sun/Moon, Eye/EyeOff, Bike, Footprints, Dumbbell.

## Voice
Spanish (es-ES), tuteo. Direct, no marketingese. "Generar 303" not "Procesar modelo trimestral del IVA". Empty states positive. Errors honest not alarming.

## Motion
- Hover: 120ms ease-out
- Tab/color: 180ms ease-out
- Side panel: 240ms ease-out
- Page transitions: 320ms ease-out
- Spring easing only for factura emitida success animation
Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

## STRICT RULES

ALWAYS:
✓ Tabular nums on every monetary amount

✓ Cmd+K from any page

✗ Zebra striping in tables
✗ Modal for row detail
✗ Multiple top tabs nav (one sidebar only)
✗ Pure white text on dark
✗ Mercury purple #6C5CE7 literal

# Design System Strategy: The Calm Enterprise

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
**The Creative North Star: "The Architectural Sanctuary"**

Standard enterprise software is often cluttered, loud, and built on rigid, boxed-in grids. This design system rejects the "dashboard-as-a-cockpit" mentality. Instead, we treat the interface as an architectural space—a sanctuary for high-stakes project work. 

Our goal is to create a "Calm Enterprise" aesthetic that feels authoritative yet breathable. We move beyond generic UI by utilizing **intentional asymmetry**, **tonal layering**, and **editorial spacing**. We prioritize the user’s cognitive load, using soft transitions and deep hierarchy to guide the eye without the "visual noise" of traditional borders and high-contrast lines.

---

## 2. Colors & Surface Logic

The palette is rooted in a "cool-neutral" spectrum, designed to reduce eye fatigue during long-duration project management tasks.

### The "No-Line" Rule
**Explicit Instruction:** Do not use 1px solid borders for primary sectioning. 
Structure is defined through background shifts. A sidebar is not "separated" by a line; it is "sunken" using the `surface-container` (#eeedf7) against the `surface` (#fbf8ff). This creates a sophisticated, modern silhouette that feels carved rather than drawn.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as physical layers of fine paper. 
- **Base Layer (Page):** `surface` (#fbf8ff).
- **Sunken Elements (Sidebars/Wells):** `surface-container` (#eeedf7).
- **Floating Elements (Cards/Modals):** `surface-container-lowest` (#ffffff).
- **Interactive Layers:** Use `surface-bright` for hover states on neutral elements to create a "glow" rather than a color change.

### The "Glass & Signature" Rule
To add soul to the enterprise experience:
- **Glassmorphism:** For top navigation or floating action panels, use `surface` at 80% opacity with a `20px backdrop-blur`. This anchors the element while maintaining a sense of space.
- **Signature Textures:** For Primary CTAs, do not use a flat hex. Apply a subtle linear gradient: `primary` (#3525cd) to `primary_container` (#4f46e5) at a 135-degree angle. This adds a "premium ink" depth to the Indigo.

---

## 3. Typography: Editorial Authority

We use **Geist Sans** (inter-token mapping) to achieve a high-end, technical-but-human feel.

| Role | Token | Size | Weight | Intent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Display** | `display-lg` | 3.5rem | 600 | Dramatic project milestones; limited use. |
| **Headline**| `headline-md`| 1.75rem| 500 | Section headers; sets the "Editorial" tone. |
| **Title**   | `title-md`   | 1.125rem| 600 | Card titles and primary navigation. |
| **Body**    | `body-md`    | 0.875rem| 400 | Primary reading; optimized for legibility. |
| **Label**   | `label-sm`   | 0.6875rem| 500 | Metadata and micro-copy; uppercase + 0.05em tracking. |

**The Hierarchy Rule:** We use "Tonal Contrast" over "Size Contrast." A `title-sm` in `on_surface` (#1a1b22) paired with `body-sm` in `on_surface_variant` (#464555) creates a clear path for the eye without requiring massive font size discrepancies.

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth: Tonal Layering

Shadows and borders are secondary to **Tonal Layering**. We communicate "up" and "down" through color depth.

- **The Layering Principle:** Place a `surface-container-lowest` (#ffffff) card on top of a `surface-container-low` (#f4f2fd) background. The 1% shift in hex value is enough for the human eye to perceive depth without the "dirtiness" of a drop shadow.
- **Ambient Shadows:** Only use shadows for "active" floating states (Modals, Popovers). Use a multi-layered shadow: 
  - `box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(26, 27, 34, 0.04), 0 10px 15px -3px rgba(26, 27, 34, 0.06);`
  - The shadow color must be a tint of `on-surface`, never pure black.
- **Ghost Borders:** For form inputs or accessibility requirements, use `outline_variant` (#c7c4d8) at **20% opacity**. It should feel like a suggestion of a boundary, not a cage.

---

## 5. Components

### Buttons
- **Primary:** Radius `10px`. Gradient fill (Indigo 600-500). White text.
- **Secondary:** Radius `10px`. `surface-container-high` background. No border. `primary` text.
- **Micro-Interaction:** On hover, buttons should shift -2px Y-axis with a subtle ambient shadow.

### Cards & Projects
- **Styling:** Radius `14px`. Background `surface-container-lowest` (#ffffff).
- **Prohibition:** No dividers. Separate header from body using a `1.5rem` (6) padding gap or a subtle shift to `surface-container-low` for the card footer.

### Inputs & Fields
- **Styling:** Radius `10px`. Background `surface-container-low`. 
- **Focus State:** 2px solid `primary` (#3525cd) with a 4px soft outer glow (10% opacity).

### Navigation (Sidebar)
- Use "Asymmetric Breathing Room." Align icons to a strict grid, but allow text labels to breathe with `1.25rem` (5) of horizontal padding. Use `surface-container` to indicate the active state, rather than a high-contrast bar.

---

## 6. Do’s and Don’ts

### Do
- **Use "Negative Space" as a layout tool.** If two elements feel cluttered, add `2rem` (8) of space instead of a line.
- **Use Lucide icons sparingly.** Stroke weight `1.75` at `18px`. Icons should be `on_surface_variant` (#464555) to remain secondary to text.
- **Embrace Asymmetry.** Align a hero title to the left while keeping a "Status" badge floating in the top right to create a sophisticated, editorial rhythm.

### Don’t
- **Never use pure black (#000000) for text.** Use `on_surface` (#1a1b22) to maintain the "Calm" aesthetic.
- **Avoid 90-degree corners.** Every interactive element must have at least a `sm` (0.25rem) radius to prevent the UI from feeling "aggressive."
- **No high-contrast dividers.** If you feel the need to "split" a page, use a background color change from the `surface` scale.

---

Design System Strategy: The Kinetic Precision Framework

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
**Creative North Star: The Performance Engine**
This design system is not a static repository of components; it is a high-performance engine for live sports data. We are moving away from the "static dashboard" trope and toward a **Kinetic Precision** aesthetic. This means the UI should feel like a broadcast overlay—fast, authoritative, and layered. 

We achieve a premium, custom feel by rejecting standard "boxed-in" layouts. Instead, we use **intentional asymmetry** and **tonal layering**. The interface doesn't just display data; it prioritizes it through a "Bento-Editorial" layout where the scale of information dictates the size of the container, creating a rhythm that feels more like a premium magazine than a spreadsheet.

---

## 2. Colors: Tonal Depth & Hierarchy
We utilize a sophisticated palette that balances the deep authority of Navy with the high-energy vibration of "Live" Red and "Action" Green.

### The "No-Line" Rule
**Borders are prohibited for sectioning.** To define boundaries, you must use background color shifts. A `surface-container-low` widget sitting on a `surface` background provides all the separation needed. High-contrast lines create visual noise; tonal shifts create focus.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as a physical stack of glass and paper:
- **Base Layer (`surface`):** The stadium floor. Everything sits here.
- **Section Layer (`surface-container-low`):** Used for grouping related content blocks.
- **Interactive Layer (`surface-container-lowest` / White):** High-priority cards that need to "pop" for user interaction.
- **Elevation Layer (`surface-bright`):** For active states or floating tooltips.

### The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
To elevate beyond the "out-of-the-box" look, use **Glassmorphism** for persistent floating elements (like a live score ticker). Use a 12px `backdrop-blur` with a semi-transparent `surface` fill. 
*   **Signature Texture:** Use a subtle linear gradient from `primary` (#006a33) to `primary_container` (#3fff8b) at a 135-degree angle for primary CTAs. This adds a "lithographic" depth that flat hex codes lack.

---

## 3. Typography: Editorial Authority
We use **Inter** not as a default, but as a precision tool. The hierarchy is designed to mimic sports journalism: massive displays for scores, and tight, high-density labels for stats.

*   **Display (lg/md):** Reserved for "Hero" moments—match scores or countdowns. Letter-spacing should be set to `-0.02em` to feel tighter and more aggressive.
*   **Headline (sm/md):** Used for section titles. These are the anchors of your Bento grid.
*   **Label (sm/md):** High-density data points (e.g., "Win Probability"). These should be in `on_surface_variant` (#535b71) and often all-caps with `+0.05em` tracking for maximum legibility at small scales.

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth: Tonal Layering
Traditional drop shadows are too "software-generic." We use **Tonal Layering** to define importance.

*   **The Layering Principle:** Instead of a shadow, place a `surface-container-lowest` (pure white) card inside a `surface-container` (#e2e7ff) wrapper. The contrast creates a natural "lift."
*   **Ambient Shadows:** For "Live" floating cards, use a shadow with a 32px blur and 4% opacity, tinted with the `on_surface` color (#272e42). It should feel like a soft glow, not a dark smudge.
*   **The Ghost Border:** If a separator is required for accessibility, use the `outline_variant` token at **15% opacity**. It should be felt, not seen.
*   **Kinetic Live State:** Elements with the `tertiary` (Red Live) color should utilize a soft, pulsing outer glow using a 10% opacity version of the same color to indicate real-time data streaming.

---

## 5. Components: High-Density Primitives

### Bento Stat Cards
- **Structure:** No borders. Use a 4px solid left-accent using `primary`, `secondary`, or `tertiary` to categorize the stat type.
- **Background:** `surface-container-lowest` (White).
- **Corner Radius:** `xl` (1.5rem / 24px) for the outer container, `md` (0.75rem / 12px) for internal nested elements.

### The "Live" Timeline
- **Interaction:** Avoid divider lines between events. Use vertical whitespace (16px) and a `surface-container-low` background on every second item to create a "Zebra" striping effect that feels organic.
- **Indicator:** Use the `tertiary_container` for the "Current Time" marker to ensure it cuts through the Navy/Green noise.

### Buttons & Inputs
- **Primary Button:** Gradient fill (`primary` to `primary_container`) with `on_primary_fixed` text. Rounded-full for a "stadium" pill shape.
- **Input Fields:** Use `surface-container-highest` for the field background. On focus, do not use a heavy border; shift the background to `surface-bright` and add a 2px `primary` bottom-border only.

### Data Visualization Cards
- **Dark Mode Inversion:** Even in Light Mode, Data Viz cards (charts/graphs) should use the `inverse_surface` (#060e20) background. This provides a "Pro" look, making the green and blue data lines vibrate with clarity against the dark void.

---

## 6. Do’s and Don’ts

### Do
- **Do** use `surface-container` tiers to nest content. An inner chart should be a different shade than its parent card.
- **Do** use asymmetric layouts. If a "Live Stream" card is 2/3 width, the "Player Stats" card should be 1/3 to create an editorial feel.
- **Do** use `display-lg` typography for the most important number on the screen.

### Don't
- **Don't** use 1px solid #HEX borders. They make the dashboard look like legacy enterprise software.
- **Don't** use pure black for text. Always use `on_surface` (#272e42) to maintain a premium, ink-like softness.
- **Don't** use standard "Drop Shadows" from a UI kit. If it’s not an ambient, tinted glow, don't use it.

## Brand & Style

The design system is rooted in the philosophy of the Mediterranean lifestyle: balance, natural abundance, and a slow, intentional pace. The visual style is **Organic Minimalism**, blending high-end editorial aesthetics with the warmth of sun-drenched coastal landscapes. 

The goal is to evoke a sense of serenity and nourishment, moving away from the cold, data-heavy interfaces common in nutrition apps toward a helpful, lifestyle-oriented companion. The interface utilizes generous whitespace, earthy tones, and soft tactile elements to build a trustworthy and premium user experience.

## Colors

The palette is derived from Mediterranean flora and earth. 
- **Background (#FBF7EE):** A warm, parchment-like cream that serves as a soft alternative to pure white, reducing eye strain and feeling more "natural."
- **Primary (#3F5B2A):** A deep olive green used for high-emphasis actions, navigation, and core branding elements to project stability and health.
- **Soft Primary (#A9AC5B):** A muted sage used for secondary actions, toggles, and decorative backgrounds.
- **Accent (#C77A3F):** A rich terracotta used sparingly for call-to-outs, nutritional highlights, or seasonal alerts.
- **Neutral/Text:** High-contrast charcoal for primary legibility and a softened slate for metadata and auxiliary labels.

## Typography

The design system utilizes **Inter** exclusively to maintain a modern, clean, and highly legible interface. To avoid a "corporate" feel, use a generous line-height (1.6 for body text) and slight negative letter spacing on larger headlines to give them a customized, editorial appearance. Headlines should be treated with a rhythmic hierarchy to guide the user through their meal planning journey without overwhelming them with information density.

## Layout & Spacing

The layout follows a **fluid grid** model tailored for mobile and tablet consumption. On mobile devices, use a 4-column grid with 20px side margins; on larger screens, transition to a centered 12-column grid. 

Vertical rhythm is governed by a 4px base unit. Spacing should be airy and open. Components should favor `lg` (24px) or `xl` (40px) vertical margins to reinforce the "calm" brand personality. Grouped items (like ingredients in a list) should use `sm` (8px) gaps.

## Elevation & Depth

This design system avoids heavy shadows in favor of **Tonal Layers and Soft Outlines**. Depth is primarily established by placing white cards (`#FFFFFF`) against the warm cream background (`#FBF7EE`). 

Where elevation is required for interactivity (e.g., a floating action button or a selected card), use a very diffused, low-opacity shadow with a slight Olive tint:
- **Shadow-SM:** 0px 2px 8px rgba(63, 91, 42, 0.05)
- **Shadow-MD:** 0px 4px 16px rgba(63, 91, 42, 0.08)

Interactive elements use a 1px border of the Primary color at 10% opacity to define boundaries without adding visual clutter.

## Shapes

The shape language is a mix of structured geometry and organic softness. 
- **Cards & Modals:** Use a consistent **16px** border radius to feel friendly but organized.
- **Buttons & Chips:** Use a **Pill-shape (999px)** to maximize the approachable, soft nature of the brand.
- **Icons:** Use outline-style icons with a **1.5px stroke weight**. Icons should have slightly rounded terminals to match the typography.
- **Images:** Food and lifestyle photography should always use the 16px radius.

## Components

- **Buttons:** Primary buttons are solid Olive Green (#3F5B2A) with white text. Secondary buttons use the Soft Primary (#A9AC5B) with a subtle cream background or an outline. All buttons are pill-shaped.
- **Cards:** Pure white (#FFFFFF) containers with 16px corner radius. Use them for meal cards, daily summaries, and recipe suggestions.
- **Chips:** Used for dietary tags (e.g., "Vegan," "High Protein"). These are small pill-shaped elements with a #A9AC5B background at 15% opacity and dark text.
- **Input Fields:** Minimalist design with a 1.5px Olive Green bottom border or a very subtle 16px rounded frame.
- **Lists:** Ingredient lists should have generous 16px vertical padding between items, separated by a light 1px divider in the secondary text color at low opacity.

Design System Document: The Precision Engineer

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
The "Precision Engineer" is a design system that rejects the cluttered "cockpit" aesthetic of traditional developer tools in favor of **Structural Serenity**. While most dev tools overwhelm the user with dense grids and harsh borders, this system treats data as editorial content. 

**Creative North Star: The Architectural Blueprint**
The interface should feel like a high-end physical workspace: clean, expansive, and organized by logic rather than lines. We move beyond the "template" look by using intentional white space as a functional tool, allowing complex code and data structures to breathe. We replace rigid boxes with **Tonal Nesting** and **Asymmetric Balance**, ensuring that even the most data-heavy dashboard feels like a premium, intentional experience.

---

## 2. Colors & Surface Logic
The palette is anchored in `Indigo-600` for primary actions, balanced against a sophisticated range of cool grays.

### The "No-Line" Rule
**Borders are a design failure.** In this system, 1px solid borders for sectioning are strictly prohibited. Boundaries must be defined through background color shifts. For example, a `surface_container_low` sidebar sitting against a `surface` main content area creates a natural, sophisticated edge without visual noise.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as a series of physical layers. Use the following tiers to create depth:
*   **Base Layer:** `surface` (#f8f9fa) – The foundation.
*   **Secondary Sections:** `surface_container_low` (#f3f4f5) – Use for sidebars or utility panels.
*   **Active Workspaces:** `surface_container_lowest` (#ffffff) – Reserved for the primary code editor or data cards to provide maximum contrast.
*   **Interactive Elements:** `surface_container_high` (#e7e8e9) – For "pushed" or active states.

### The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
To elevate the "out-of-the-box" Indigo-600, apply a subtle linear gradient to primary buttons and hero states (Transitioning from `primary` #3525cd to `primary_container` #4f46e5 at a 135° angle). For floating overlays or command palettes, use **Glassmorphism**: `surface_container_lowest` at 80% opacity with a `24px` backdrop-blur.

---

## 3. Typography
We use **Inter** for its mathematical precision. The hierarchy is designed to be "Editorial Developer"—high contrast between metadata and primary data.

*   **Display & Headlines:** Use `display-md` for high-level metrics. It should feel authoritative.
*   **The Metadata Scale:** Use `label-md` and `label-sm` in `on_surface_variant` for timestamps, commit hashes, and logs. This creates a clear distinction between "The Content" and "The Data About the Content."
*   **The Code Contrast:** While UI labels use standard Inter, any dynamic developer data (IDs, endpoints) should use a monospaced variant of Inter or a system mono font to signal "Interactivity" vs "Static Label."

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth
Depth is achieved through **Tonal Layering** rather than structural scaffolding.

*   **The Layering Principle:** Instead of a shadow, place a `surface_container_lowest` (White) card on a `surface_container_low` background. The slight shift in hex value provides a sophisticated "lift."
*   **Ambient Shadows:** When an element must float (e.g., a dropdown or modal), use an ultra-diffused shadow: `box-shadow: 0 20px 40px rgba(25, 28, 29, 0.05)`. The shadow must be a tinted version of the `on_surface` color, never pure black.
*   **The Ghost Border Fallback:** If a container sits on a background of the same color, use a **Ghost Border**: `outline_variant` at 15% opacity. It should be felt, not seen.

---

## 5. Components

### Cards
*   **Radius:** `xl` (1.5rem / 24px) for main containers; `lg` (1rem / 16px) for nested content.
*   **Rule:** Forbid divider lines. Use `1.5rem` of vertical padding and a background shift to `surface_container_low` to separate header from body.

### Buttons
*   **Primary:** Indigo gradient with `on_primary` text. `radius-md`.
*   **Secondary:** `surface_container_high` background with `on_surface` text. No border.
*   **Tertiary:** Transparent background, `primary` text. Use only for low-emphasis actions like "Cancel."

### Input Fields
*   **State:** Default state uses `surface_container_low` with no border. On focus, the background shifts to `surface_container_lowest` with a 2px `primary` Ghost Border (20% opacity).

### Specialized Dev Components
*   **Status Indicators:** Instead of a simple dot, use a `tertiary_container` pill with `on_tertiary_fixed_variant` text for "Pending" and `error_container` for "Failed."
*   **Log Streams:** Use `surface_container_highest` for the container background to simulate a terminal feel within the light-mode ecosystem.

---

## 6. Do’s and Don'ts

### Do:
*   **Do** use asymmetrical layouts. A wide primary column for code and a narrow right-aligned column for metadata creates a modern, editorial feel.
*   **Do** prioritize `title-sm` for card headers to keep the interface feeling professional and compact.
*   **Do** use `primary_fixed` for subtle highlights in tables or lists to draw the eye without overwhelming the user.

### Don’t:
*   **Don't** use 1px gray borders to separate list items. Use white space or a 4px gap.
*   **Don't** use pure black (#000). Always use `on_surface` (#191c1d) to maintain the premium light-mode softness.

Design System Strategy: The Architectural Clinician

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
The design system is built upon the "Architectural Clinician" North Star. This philosophy rejects the cluttered, "boxed-in" aesthetic typical of legacy medical software. Instead, we embrace a high-end editorial approach that mirrors the precision of modern dentistry: clean, structural, and impeccably sterile without feeling cold.

We move beyond the "standard SaaS" look by utilizing intentional asymmetry, high-scale typographic breathing room, and a depth model based on tonal layering rather than rigid borders. The experience should feel like a custom-designed laboratory—where every element has a logical placement and the UI recedes to let the data (and the clinician’s expertise) take center stage.

---

## 2. Color & Surface Logic
The palette is rooted in a deep, authoritative Indigo. However, the premium feel is derived not from the color itself, but from the **Surface Hierarchy**.

### The "No-Line" Rule
To achieve "Clinical Precision," we forbid the use of 1px solid borders for sectioning. Structural boundaries must be defined solely through background shifts.
*   **The Logic:** If a section needs to be separated, move from `surface` (#fbf8ff) to `surface-container-low` (#f4f2fe).
*   **The Result:** A layout that feels carved from a single block of marble rather than stitched together from disparate boxes.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as a series of physical layers—like stacked sheets of frosted glass.
*   **Base:** `surface` (#fbf8ff) for the main canvas.
*   **Structural Tiers:** Use `surface-container` (#eeecf8) for sidebars and `surface-container-highest` (#e3e1ed) for active navigation states.
*   **The Depth Play:** Nested cards should use `surface-container-lowest` (#ffffff) on top of `surface-container-low` (#f4f2fe) backgrounds to create a soft, natural "lift."

### The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
To avoid a flat, "out-of-the-box" appearance:
*   **Glassmorphism:** Use `surface` colors at 80% opacity with a `20px backdrop-blur` for floating modals and navigation bars.
*   **Signature Textures:** Apply a subtle linear gradient (from `primary` #2d009c to `primary_container` #4310d1) on primary CTAs and hero data visualizations to provide a sense of "visual soul."

---

## 3. Typography: Editorial Precision
We use **Public Sans** exclusively. Its neutral, grotesque DNA provides the "Medical Precision" required, but our implementation follows an editorial scale to create a sense of luxury.

*   **Display (Large/Medium):** Reserved for high-level clinic metrics. These should be tracked slightly tighter (-0.02em) to feel like an architectural masthead.
*   **Headlines & Titles:** Use `headline-sm` (1.5rem) for section headers. Always pair these with generous top-padding to allow the "Architectural" space to breathe.
*   **Body & Labels:** `body-md` (0.875rem) is our workhorse. For clinical data or metadata, use `label-md` (0.75rem) in `on_surface_variant` (#484555) to maintain a clear hierarchy without visual noise.

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth
Elevation is achieved through **Tonal Layering**, not structural lines.

*   **The Layering Principle:** Stacking tiers (Lowest on top of Low) creates a sophisticated, "quiet" depth.
*   **Ambient Shadows:** For floating elements (Modals, Popovers), use extra-diffused shadows.
    *   *Spec:* `0px 20px 40px rgba(26, 27, 35, 0.06)` (A tinted version of `on-surface`). Never use pure black shadows.
*   **The "Ghost Border" Fallback:** If accessibility requires a border (e.g., input fields), use `outline_variant` (#c9c4d8) at **20% opacity**. High-contrast, 100% opaque borders are strictly prohibited.

---

## 5. Components

### Buttons
*   **Primary:** Gradient fill (`primary` to `primary_container`), `lg` (0.5rem) roundness. No border.
*   **Secondary:** `surface_container_high` background with `on_secondary_container` text.
*   **Tertiary:** No background. Text-only with a hover state that utilizes a subtle `surface_bright` tint.

### Input Fields
*   **Styling:** Forgo the "boxed" input. Use a `surface_container_low` background with a `md` (0.375rem) radius and a `Ghost Border` that transitions to a 2px `primary` bottom-edge highlight on focus.

### Cards & Lists
*   **The Separation Rule:** Forbid divider lines. Separate list items using vertical white space from the spacing scale (e.g., 16px) or by alternating background tints between `surface` and `surface_container_lowest`.

### Chips (Clinical Status)
*   **Precision Tags:** Use `surface_container_high` with `label-sm` caps-styled text. For status indicators (e.g., "In-Surgery"), use the `tertiary` (#5e1600) and `tertiary_fixed` (#ffdbd1) tokens to provide a sophisticated, muted urgency.

### Contextual Components for Dental SaaS
*   **The "Tooth Map" Interface:** Use Glassmorphism for overlays on dental charts.
*   **Timeline Progress:** Instead of a line, use a series of staggered `surface_container_highest` blocks to indicate appointment progression.

---

## 6. Do’s and Don’ts

### Do:
*   **Do** use asymmetrical layouts. Let a sidebar be wide and a content area be tightly centered to create an editorial feel.
*   **Do** utilize `primary_fixed_dim` (#c8bfff) for subtle highlights in complex data tables.
*   **Do** prioritize "Active White Space." If a screen feels crowded, increase the padding—don't add a border.

### Don’t:
*   **Don't** use 1px solid dividers to separate content. Use a `4px` height `surface_container` block or simple white space.
*   **Don't** use standard "Drop Shadows" from a UI kit. Always tint your shadows with the `on_surface` token.
*   **Don't** use high-saturation reds for errors. # Design System Strategy: The Culinary Architect

This design system is built for a high-end SaaS environment where precision meets hospitality. We are moving away from the "industrial spreadsheet" aesthetic of traditional cost management and toward a "Digital Sommelier" experience: authoritative, warm, and impeccably organized.

---

### 1. Creative North Star: The Organic Ledger
The "Organic Ledger" philosophy treats the UI not as a digital grid, but as a series of premium paper stocks layered on a chef’s marble countertop. We avoid the rigid, boxed-in look of standard software by using **tonal depth** and **asymmetric breathing room**. The interface should feel as intentional and high-quality as a Michelin-star menu.

**Key Principles:**
- **Intentional Negative Space:** We use wide gutters and generous padding to ensure complex financial data never feels claustrophobic.
- **Warm Precision:** While the math is cold and hard, the interface is soft and inviting, utilizing the amber-based palette to reduce eye strain during long inventory sessions.

---

### 2. Colors & Surface Philosophy

The color palette is rooted in Earth tones and harvest ambers, moving away from "SaaS Blue" to establish a signature identity in the hospitality tech space.

#### The "No-Line" Rule
**Standard 1px borders are strictly prohibited for layout sectioning.** To define boundaries, designers must use background color shifts. 
- *Example:* A recipe detail panel (`surface-container-low`) should sit directly on the main application background (`surface`) without a stroke. The transition of color is the border.

#### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as a physical stack of materials. Use the following tiers to create depth:
- **Base Layer:** `surface` (#faf9f7) - The "tabletop."
- **Sectioning:** `surface-container-low` (#f4f3f1) - Use for large sidebar or background zones.
- **Interactive Elements:** `surface-container` (#efeeec) - Use for the "paper" that holds content.
- **Elevated Cards:** `surface-container-lowest` (#ffffff) - Reserved for the highest-level focal points, like the 480px centered cost cards.

#### Glass & Gradient Signature
For floating action buttons or high-level navigation overlays, use **Glassmorphism**. Apply `surface` with 80% opacity and a `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)`. To add "soul," primary buttons should use a subtle linear gradient: `primary` (#8d4b00) to `primary_container` (#b15f00) at a 135° angle.

---

### 3. Typography: The Editorial Scale

We use **Work Sans** exclusively. Its optimized legibility and modern geometric construction provide a "clean-slate" feel essential for financial auditing.

*   **Display (lg/md):** Reserved for high-level dashboard metrics (e.g., Total Food Cost %). Use `-0.02em` letter spacing to give it an editorial, "heavyweight" feel.
*   **Headline (sm/md):** Used for recipe names and section headers. High contrast against the background is key.
*   **Body (md/lg):** The workhorse for ingredient lists and cost breakdowns. Use `on_surface_variant` (#554336) for secondary body text to soften the visual weight.
*   **Label (sm/md):** All-caps with `+0.05em` letter spacing for table headers or metadata to distinguish them clearly from data.

---

### 4. Elevation & Depth

We eschew traditional "box shadows" in favor of **Tonal Layering**.

*   **The Layering Principle:** Place a `surface-container-lowest` card on a `surface-container-low` section. This 1-step shift in value provides enough contrast for the human eye to perceive elevation without visual noise.
*   **Ambient Shadows:** For the 480px centered cards, use a shadow with a 40px blur, 0px offset, and 6% opacity using the `on_surface` color (#1a1c1b). This mimics soft, natural kitchen lighting.
*   **The "Ghost Border" Fallback:** If accessibility requires a stroke (e.g., in high-glare environments), use `outline_variant` (#dbc2b0) at **15% opacity**. Never use a 100% opaque border.

---

### 5. Components & Interaction

#### Buttons
- **Primary:** Gradient-filled (Amber tones), 12px radius. No border. Text is `on_primary` (#ffffff).
- **Secondary:** `surface-container-high` background with `primary` colored text.
- **Tertiary:** No background. Subtle `primary` text. Use for low-priority actions like "Cancel."

#### Inputs & Fields
- **Design:** Forgo the 4-sided box. Use a `surface-container-highest` background with a 12px top-radius and a 2px `primary` bottom-stroke only upon focus.
- **Validation:** Error states use `error` (#ba1a1a) text but the background container should shift to `error_container` (#ffdad6) at 30% opacity.

#### Cards & Lists
- **The Divider Ban:** Never use horizontal lines to separate list items (e.g., ingredients). Use `8px` of vertical white space (Spacing Scale 2) and a subtle hover state shift to `surface-container-high`.
- **The 480px Center Card:** The signature component for this system. It must be centered with `24px` padding, 12px radius, and use the "Ambient Shadow" for focus.

- **The "Cost-Badge":** A pill-shaped chip using `tertiary_container` for positive margin items and `error_container` for high-waste items.

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
**Creative North Star: "The Clinical Curator"**
The dental industry demands a duality of character: the clinical sterility of a medical environment and the high-end comfort of a premium practice. This design system moves beyond the "generic SaaS dashboard" by adopting an editorial layout strategy. We replace rigid, boxed-in grids with **Intentional Asymmetry** and **Atmospheric Depth**. 

The goal is to make data feel curated, not just displayed. We achieve this through expansive white space, overlapping "glass" layers, and a sophisticated typographic scale that treats patient analytics with the same prestige as a high-end medical journal.

---

## 2. Colors & Surface Philosophy
The palette is rooted in a "High-Value White" foundation, utilizing the Material Design convention to create a sophisticated hierarchy without relying on heavy lines.

### The "No-Line" Rule
**Borders are a failure of hierarchy.** In this system, 1px solid borders are strictly prohibited for sectioning. Differentiation must be achieved through:
- **Tonal Shifts:** Placing a `surface-container-lowest` card (#ffffff) on a `surface-container-low` (#f3f4f5) background.
- **Negative Space:** Using the Spacing Scale to create "void-boundaries."

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as physical layers of frosted glass and fine vellum.
- **Level 0 (Base):** `surface` (#f8f9fa) — The infinite canvas.
- **Level 1 (Sections):** `surface-container-low` (#f3f4f5) — Large logical groupings.
- **Level 2 (Active Cards):** `surface-container-lowest` (#ffffff) — The primary interactive layer.

### The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
To inject "soul" into the data, use `surface_tint` (#4d44e3) at 5-10% opacity with a `backdrop-blur` of 12px for floating modals or navigation overlays. Main CTAs should utilize a linear gradient: `primary` (#3525cd) to `primary_container` (#4f46e5) at a 135° angle to create a sense of tactile energy.

---

## 3. Typography: The Editorial Voice
We use a dual-sans serif approach to balance authority with readability.

- **Display & Headlines (Manrope):** Chosen for its geometric precision and modern "medical-tech" feel. Use `display-md` for high-level KPI totals to give them a "hero" presence.
- **Body & Labels (Inter):** The workhorse. Inter’s tall x-height ensures patient data and chart labels remain legible even at `label-sm` (11px).

**The Hierarchy Rule:** Always pair a `headline-sm` (Manrope) with a `label-md` (Inter, All Caps, 0.05em tracking) to create a clear "Title/Subtitle" relationship that feels like a premium publication.

We eschew the "standard drop shadow" in favor of **Ambient Luminance.**

### The Layering Principle
Depth is achieved by "stacking" tones. 
*Example:* A `surface-container-lowest` card sits on a `surface-container-low` background. To the eye, the card "lifts" naturally because it is the brightest element.

### Ambient Shadows
When a card requires a floating state (e.g., a hovered KPI card), use an extra-diffused shadow:
- **X: 0, Y: 8px, Blur: 24px.**
- **Color:** `on-surface` (#191c1d) at **4% opacity**.
- This mimics natural light passing through a dental office window, rather than a digital "glow."

### The "Ghost Border" Fallback
If contrast ratios fail in specific edge cases, use a **Ghost Border**: `outline-variant` (#c7c4d8) at **15% opacity**. Never use a 100% opaque border.

Design System Specification: Technical Precision & Atmospheric Depth

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star: "The Kinetic Engine"
The Creative North Star for this design system is **"The Kinetic Engine."** 

We are moving away from the static, "boxed-in" layout of traditional SaaS templates. Instead, we treat the UI as a high-performance machine—precise, ventilated, and layered. The aesthetic draws from the technical rigor of terminal interfaces and the atmospheric depth of high-end editorial photography. 

To achieve this, we utilize **Intentional Asymmetry**. Do not feel forced to center every hero element; allow "on-surface" content to bleed off-edge or sit offset to create a sense of forward motion. We use generous whitespace (specifically scales `16` to `24`) to give technical data room to breathe, ensuring the complexity of the "SpecBox Engine" feels manageable and premium.

---

## 2. Colors: Tonal Architecture
This system rejects the "flat" dark mode. We build interfaces through light and depth, not lines.

### Palette Strategy
- **Base:** `surface` (#071325) is our infinite void.
- **Primary:** `primary` (#abc7ff) and `primary_container` (#438fff) act as the "Electric Blue" pulse. Use these for high-action focal points only.
- **Secondary:** `secondary` (#b9c8de) provides a muted, technical slate feel for supporting information.

### The "No-Line" Rule
**Explicit Instruction:** Designers are prohibited from using 1px solid borders for sectioning or layout containment. Structural boundaries must be defined solely through background color shifts. 
*   *Example:* A feature grid should sit on `surface_container_low`, while the individual feature cards use `surface_container`. The distinction is felt through the shift in depth, not a hard line.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as stacked sheets of obsidian glass.
1.  **Level 0 (Background):** `surface`
2.  **Level 1 (Sections):** `surface_container_low`
3.  **Level 2 (Cards/Modules):** `surface_container` or `surface_container_high`
4.  **Level 3 (Floating Menus):** `surface_container_highest` with a `surface_tint` overlay at 5%.

### The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
To escape the "flat" look, use Glassmorphism for floating navigation and modals. 
*   **Formula:** `surface_container_low` at 70% opacity + 20px Backdrop Blur.
*   **Signature Textures:** Apply a linear gradient (45deg) from `primary_container` to `primary` for main CTAs to give them a "lit from within" glow.

---

## 3. Typography: Editorial Authority
The interplay between **Plus Jakarta Sans** (Display) and **Inter** (Functional) creates a balance between "Tech-Chic" and "Engineered Reliability."

*   **Display Scale (`display-lg` to `display-sm`):** Reserved for high-impact marketing claims. Use `display-lg` (3.5rem) with tight letter-spacing (-0.04em) to create a "block" of text that feels like a physical object.
*   **Headline Scale (`headline-lg` to `headline-sm`):** Use for section headers. Always pair with `secondary_text` (Slate Light) body copy to maintain high-contrast hierarchy.
*   **The Technical Label:** `label-md` and `label-sm` should often be set in uppercase with +0.1em letter spacing. These are your "data points" and should feel like code snippets or serial numbers.

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth: Tonal Layering
We do not use shadows to represent "drop." We use them to represent "ambient glow."

*   **The Layering Principle:** Depth is achieved by stacking. Place `surface_container_lowest` cards on a `surface_container_low` background to create a "recessed" look, or vice versa for a "lifted" look.
*   **Ambient Shadows:** For floating elements, use a `24px` blur with 6% opacity. The shadow color must be `primary_fixed_dim` to simulate the blue light of the interface reflecting off the surface.
*   **The Ghost Border:** If a border is required for accessibility (e.g., input fields), use `outline_variant` at **15% opacity**. Never use 100% opaque borders.
*   **Glassmorphism:** Navigation bars must use `surface_dim` with a `0.175rem` (0.5 scale) "rim light" on the top edge only, using `outline_variant` at 20% opacity.

---

## 5. Components: The Primitive Set

### Buttons (The Kinetic Triggers)
- **Primary:** Gradient from `primary_container` to `primary`. No border. White text (`on_primary_container`). `xl` (0.75rem) roundedness.
- **Secondary:** `surface_container_high` background with a `ghost border`. Text color: `primary`.
- **Tertiary:** Pure text with an underline that appears on hover. Use `title-sm` for weight.

### Input Fields
- **Base:** `surface_container_lowest` background. 
- **State:** On focus, the border (ghost border) increases to 40% opacity of `primary`, and a subtle `surface_tint` outer glow (4px) is applied.
- **Error:** Use `error` (#ffb4ab) only for the helper text and a 1px bottom-only border.

### Cards & Lists
- **Rule:** **No Dividers.** 
- Use the `Spacing Scale (8)` to separate list items. 
- For cards, use a subtle background shift from `surface_container` to `surface_container_high` on hover to indicate interactivity.

### Engineering-Specific Components
- **The Spec-Badge:** Use `tertiary_container` for badges indicating "Beta" or "Technical Specs." This orange-tinted hue provides a necessary "warning/alert" contrast to the deep navy and blue.
- **The Monospace Readout:** For engine specs, use `label-md` but swap the font-family to a monospace equivalent to signify raw data.

Design System Strategy: BeatBook

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
**The Creative North Star: "The Sonic Architect"**

The design system is built to transform a management tool into a high-end performance instrument. We are moving beyond the "utility app" aesthetic to create a "Sonic Architect" experience: a layout that feels as precise as a MIDI controller and as atmospheric as a dimly lit club.

The system breaks the "template" look by utilizing **intentional asymmetry** and **tonal depth**. Rather than a standard dashboard, the interface behaves like an editorial spread for the music industry—high-contrast typography scales meet deep, layered surfaces to create a sense of professional authority and "minimal luxury."

---

## 2. Colors & Surface Philosophy
The palette is rooted in the "After Hours" spectrum—deep indigos and charcoals that allow the primary violet accent to vibrate with energy.

### Core Palette
- **Background (`surface`):** `#0e0e13` – The foundation. Deep, infinite, and immersive.
- **Primary Accent (`primary`):** `#aca3ff` – Used for moments of high-intent and brand signature.
- **Secondary (`secondary`):** `#b190fe` – Reserved for tonal shifts in interactive elements.
- **Surface Tiers:**
    - `surface_container_low`: `#131318`
    - `surface_container`: `#19191f`
    - `surface_container_high`: `#1f1f26`

### The "No-Line" Rule
To achieve a premium, seamless feel, designers are prohibited from using 1px solid borders for sectioning. Structural boundaries must be defined solely through background color shifts. For example, a tracklist (using `surface_container_low`) should sit directly on the `surface` background without a stroke. Use the **Spacing Scale (Token 8 or 10)** to create breathing room that defines the edge.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as a series of physical layers. 
- **The Base:** The main application background (`surface`).
- **The Deck:** Major content areas use `surface_container`.
- **The Module:** Interactive cards or nested elements use `surface_container_high`.
Each inner container should use a slightly higher tier to define its importance, creating a "stacked" feel that mimics expensive hardware.

### The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
For floating elements like "Now Playing" bars or modal overlays, use **Glassmorphism**. Combine `surface_container_highest` at 70% opacity with a `20px` backdrop-blur. Apply a subtle linear gradient to main CTAs (transitioning from `primary` to `primary_dim`) to provide a visual "soul" that flat colors cannot achieve.

---

## 3. Typography
We use **Inter** not just for legibility, but as a geometric design element.

- **Display (display-lg/md):** Use for "Hero" moments like Venue Names or Monthly Earnings. These should be `font-weight: 700` with tight tracking (`-0.02em`) to mimic high-end editorial magazines.
- **Headlines (headline-sm):** Used for section titles. Always paired with high vertical white space to command attention.
- **Body (body-md):** The workhorse. Set to `on_surface_variant` (`#acaab1`) to reduce eye strain during long set-planning sessions.
- **Labels (label-sm):** All-caps with `0.05em` letter spacing. Use these for metadata (BPM, Key, Genre) to create a technical, "data-rich" aesthetic.

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth

### The Layering Principle
Depth is achieved through **Tonal Layering**. Avoid structural lines; instead, place a `surface_container_lowest` card on a `surface_container_low` section. This creates a soft, natural lift that feels integrated into the environment.

### Ambient Shadows
When a component must float (e.g., a context menu), use a "Sonic Shadow":
- **Color:** `surface_container_lowest` (Black) at 40% opacity.
- **Blur:** 30px - 50px.
- **Spread:** -5px.
This creates a soft glow of "absence" rather than a harsh drop shadow.

### The "Ghost Border" Fallback
If a border is required for accessibility (e.g., input fields), use the **Ghost Border**: the `outline_variant` token at **15% opacity**. High-contrast, 100% opaque borders are strictly forbidden as they break the luxury "dark-mode" immersion.

---

## 5. Components

### Buttons
- **Primary:** Gradient fill (`primary` to `primary_dim`). `border-radius: full` for a modern, sleek feel.
- **Secondary:** Ghost style. No fill, `outline_variant` at 20% opacity.
- **Interaction:** On hover, the button should "glow"—add a subtle outer shadow using the `primary` color at 10% opacity.

### Cards & Lists
- **Rule:** Forbid the use of divider lines between list items. Use **Vertical White Space (Token 4)** to separate tracks or bookings.
- **Visual Style:** Cards use `border-radius: 14px` (`lg`) and the Ghost Border. The background should be `surface_container`.

### Input Fields
- **State:** Active inputs use a 1px border of `primary` at 50% opacity. 
- **Typography:** Placeholder text must be `on_surface_variant` to maintain the dark hierarchy.

### Special App Components: "The Performance Deck"
- **BPM Slider:** A custom range input using the `primary` color for the track and `on_primary` for the handle.
- **Waveform Display:** Use a secondary-to-tertiary gradient to visualize audio peaks, ensuring the "energy" of the music is reflected in the UI.

---

## 6. Do’s and Don’ts

### Do:
- **Use Asymmetry:** Place a large Display-scale title on the left and a small metadata Label-sm on the right to create a "Linear" inspired professional tension.
- **Embrace Negative Space:** If a screen feels crowded, increase the padding using the **Spacing Scale (Token 12 or 16)**. Luxury is defined by the space you don't use.
- **Color Triage:** Use the `primary` accent sparingly. It should act as a "laser" that guides the eye to the most important action on the screen.

### Don’t:
- **Don’t use White:** Pure white (#FFFFFF) is too harsh. Always use `on_background` (#f8f5fd) for text to maintain the "dark room" vibe.
- **Don’t use sharp corners:** Every interactive element must use the **Roundedness Scale** (minimum `0.5rem`). Sharp corners feel utilitarian; rounded corners feel premium.

Design System Specification: The Engineering Editorial

## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
**Creative North Star: "The Architect’s Blueprint"**

This design system is built for the elite technical tier. It rejects the "bubbly" consumer web in favor of a high-precision, engineered aesthetic. It is designed to feel like a high-end IDE or a sophisticated terminal—precise, systematic, and intentional. 

To break the "template" look, we utilize **Intentional Asymmetry**. Instead of centered, predictable layouts, we favor "Command Line" alignments: heavy left-aligned typography balanced by expansive negative space or technical data visualizations on the right. We treat white space not as "empty" but as a structural component, using a rigid 4px baseline grid to ensure every element feels mathematically placed rather than "styled."

---

## 2. Colors: Deep Code
The palette is rooted in the "Deep Code" ethos—high-contrast, syntactical, and focused.

### Core Tones
- **Primary (Deep Indigo):** `#1E1B4B` (as `primary_container`). This is the foundation of our structural depth.
- **Secondary/Tertiary (Electric Teal):** `#4CD7F6` (as `secondary`). Use this sparingly for "Actionable Logic"—it represents the "cursor" or the "active state" in a sea of data.
- **Neutral Surface:** From `surface_container_lowest` (`#0E0E10`) to `surface_bright` (`#39393B`).

### The "No-Line" Rule
Traditional 1px solid borders for sectioning are strictly prohibited. Boundaries between major content blocks must be defined solely through background color shifts. 
*   *Implementation:* A `surface_container_low` section should sit flush against a `surface` background. The shift in hex value is the border.

### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
Treat the UI as a series of physical "Substrates."
- **Level 0 (Background):** `#131315` – The desk surface.
- **Level 1 (Sections):** `surface_container_low` – The main workspace.
- **Level 2 (Modules):** `surface_container` – Nested logic blocks.
- **Level 3 (Popovers/Modals):** `surface_container_highest` – Floating execution layers.

### Signature Textures
To provide "soul" to the geometric rigidity, use **Code-Syntax Decorative Motifs**. Small snippets of teal (`secondary`) or indigo (`primary`) text strings (e.g., `const build = true;`) can be used at 10% opacity as subtle background watermarks or "edge decorations."

---

## 3. Typography: Technical Authority
Typography is our primary tool for conveying "Senior-Level" expertise.

*   **Display & Headlines (JetBrains Mono):** Use for all titles. The monospace nature communicates engineering precision. Bold weight is mandatory for `display-lg` through `headline-sm`. Letter spacing should be set to `-0.02em` to keep the mono-spacing from feeling too airy.
*   **Body & Labels (Inter):** High-readability sans-serif for all functional text. Inter provides the "editorial" contrast to the "technical" mono headlines.
*   **Hierarchy Note:** Use a drastic scale jump. A `display-lg` headline (3.5rem) should often sit directly above a `label-md` (0.75rem) sub-headline to create a sophisticated, non-traditional visual rhythm.

---

## 4. Elevation & Depth: Tonal Layering
We do not use structural lines to define depth; we use "Optical Stacking."

*   **The Layering Principle:** Depth is achieved by "stacking" surface tiers. Place a `surface_container_lowest` card on a `surface_container_low` section to create a "recessed" look. 
*   **The "Ghost Border" Fallback:** If a container requires a border for accessibility (e.g., input fields), use the `outline_variant` token at **15% opacity**. This creates a "hairline" effect that feels like a laser-etched guide rather than a box.
*   **Glassmorphism & Depth:** For floating navigation or tooltips, use `surface_container_highest` at 80% opacity with a `20px` backdrop blur. This allows the "Deep Code" indigo tones to bleed through, maintaining the color story while providing clear elevation.
*   **Ambient Shadows:** Avoid "Drop Shadows." Use "Ambient Glows." Shadows must use a 4% opacity of the `on_surface` color with a `48px` blur and `0px` offset, creating a soft atmospheric lift.

---

## 5. Components: The Primitive Set

### Buttons (The "Logic Gates")
*   **Primary:** Solid `secondary` (Electric Teal) with `on_secondary` text. Corner radius: `sm` (0.125rem) for a sharp, "machined" look.
*   **Secondary:** `outline_variant` (Ghost Border) with no fill.
*   **Tertiary:** JetBrains Mono text with a trailing `_` underscore (e.g., `VIEW_DOCS_`).

### Input Fields
Strictly geometric. No rounded corners beyond `sm` (0.125rem). 
*   **State:** The "Active" state should not change the border color to a new hue, but rather increase the `outline_variant` opacity from 15% to 80% and add a subtle `secondary_container` inner glow.

### Cards & Lists
*   **The "Divider" Ban:** Forbid 100% width divider lines. Instead, use a `12` (3rem) spacing gap or a subtle shift from `surface_container` to `surface_container_high`.
*   **Syntax Chips:** Use `secondary_container` with `on_secondary_container` text. These should look like IDE tags—all caps, monospace font.

### Grid Overlays (Special Component)
For hero sections or large "empty" areas, overlay a subtle `1px` grid pattern using `outline_variant` at 5% opacity. This reinforces the "engineered" visual language.

---

## 6. Do's and Don'ts

### Do:
*   **Use Mono for Numbers:** Always use JetBrains Mono for data, dates, and metrics.
*   **Embrace the Grid:** Align everything to the 4px/8px increments. If an element is off by 1px, the "precision" feel is lost.
*   **Nesting:** Nest containers to create depth. A `surface_container_high` card inside a `surface_container_low` section is the standard.

### Don't:
*   **No Gradients:** We use solid color shifts. Gradients feel "soft"; we want "hard-edged."

a modern Bento Box layout, featuring an asymmetric grid designed for clarity and visual interest, especially on desktop. Cards are expansive and clearly defined, utilizing a `rounded-lg` (12px) border radius to soften their appearance while maintaining a contemporary feel, closely aligning with the requested 16px radius for a premium, tactile quality. Employ a nuanced depth model: surfaces subtly lift from the background with a soft, diffused `shadow-md` drop shadow, suggesting a gentle tactility. Interactive elements, especially BentoCards, will slightly `scale(1.02)` on hover with an accompanying increase to `shadow-lg`, providing clear feedback. The Hero Calendar, as the central focal point, will feature a more pronounced `shadow-xl` to emphasize its importance. 

The color story is a refined blend of fresh greens and sophisticated neutrals. The primary green, `#5DB075` (HSL: [137, 34, 53]), serves as the brand's energetic heartbeat, used prominently for all primary Call-to-Actions (CTAs), interactive elements like buttons and switches, active navigation states, and to highlight key performance metrics or progress. A darker accent green, `#3D7A4A` (HSL: [137, 34, 35]), is used for text on green backgrounds or deeper accents, while a lighter green, `#8BC49E` (HSL: [137, 34, 66]), offers subtle variations. Backgrounds in light mode are a pristine `#FAFAFA` (HSL: [0, 0, 98]), providing a clean canvas, with cards and surface elements in pure white `#FFFFFF` (HSL: [0, 0, 100]). Text is set in a legible slate `#2D4A5E` (HSL: [209, 34, 27]). In dark mode, the background transitions to a deep, immersive `#1A1A2E` (HSL: [240, 39, 14]), maintaining contrast and readability. The Hero Calendar and Next Match Card feature a dynamic gradient of the primary and dark green (`linear-gradient(135deg, #5DB075 0%, #3D7A4A 100%)`) to create visual depth and a premium feel. 

Typography relies on the modern and balanced `manrope` family, ensuring clarity and professionalism. Headlines will use `manrope` in `font-bold` or `font-extrabold` with moderate letter-spacing to command attention, while body copy and data labels will utilize `manrope` in `font-normal` or `font-medium` for optimal readability. Contrast levels will be high for textual hierarchy, ensuring important information is immediately scannable. 

Primary navigation for quick actions will be presented as a horizontal row of distinct circular icon-label components on desktop. For mobile, a compact, always-visible Floating Action Button (FAB) provides instant access to key actions. The main dashboard header includes a personalized greeting and a sleek date badge, maintaining a clean, information-rich top bar. 

Iconography will primarily leverage `Material Symbols`, chosen for their clarity and modern aesthetic. Icons will be used in both outline and filled styles depending on context (e.g., filled for active states, outlined for inactive). Imagery will be minimalist, focusing on data visualization for metrics and clear, functional graphics where needed. Spot illustrations for empty states or celebratory moments will adopt a clean, vector-based style with a limited palette, drawing from the green accent colors. 

A generous approach to spacing and negative space is adopted to enhance readability and ensure a premium, uncluttered feel. Consistent `padding-4` (`16px`) to `padding-6` (`24px`) will be applied within cards and sections, allowing content to breathe. The Bento Box layout naturally promotes spatial separation between modules, contributing to an organized and easily digestible information density. 

The overall aesthetic marries the structured modularity of 'Bento Box' design with a 'Modern Sporting Elegance'. # Potencial Digital 2026 — Design System

## Marca
- Claim: "Activa tu potencial" | Hashtag: #PotencialDigital2026
- 3er Congreso Extremeño de Transformación Digital, IA y Ciberseguridad
- Tono: Educativo, Directo, Atrevido, Digital

## Modo visual
- Dark mode nativo (fondo #000000 o #121212)
- Alta saturación, colores vibrantes sobre fondo oscuro
- Estética tecnológica con toques flúor

## Colores
- Primary: #1400C5 (azul eléctrico) — fondos, iconos, brand
- Secondary: #FF4A1F (naranja vivo) — impacto, gradientes, fotografía
- Tertiary: #09EBE1 (cyan) — acentos tecnológicos, detalles
- Accent/CTA: #E1FF2D (amarillo flúor) — botones, highlights, CTAs
- Error: #FF2E63 (rosa neón) — errores, alertas
- Surface: #121212 — cards, modals
- On Surface: #FFFFFF — texto principal

## Tipografía (en app Flutter se usan las fuentes reales)
- Display/Headlines: Lemon (custom, condensada, industrial) → en Stitch: Montserrat Black/ExtraBold
- Body/UI: Darker Grotesque → en Stitch: DM Sans

## Responsive — 3 breakpoints obligatorios
- Mobile: < 600px (1 columna, bottom nav, touch targets 48px)
- Tablet: 600-1024px (2 columnas, rail nav, densidad media)
- Desktop: > 1024px (3+ columnas, side nav, densidad alta, hover states)

## Componentes clave
- Cards con borde sutil (#1E1E1E) sobre fondo #121212
- Botones primarios: fondo #E1FF2D (flúor), texto #000000
- Botones secundarios: borde #1400C5, texto #FFFFFF
- Inputs: fondo #1A1A1A, borde #333333, focus #1400C5
- AppBar: transparente o #000000 con blur
- Bottom Nav: #121212 con iconos #FFFFFF, activo #E1FF2D

## Fotografía
- Personajes IA con iluminación cinematográfica naranja/azul/cyan
- Retratos sobre fondo negro, contraste dramático
- Diversidad de edad y género

## Recursos gráficos
- Patrones geométricos modulares (círculos concéntricos, radiantes)
- Gradientes de barras verticales (naranja-negro, cyan-negro, rosa-azul)
- Tipografía como arte (claim como pieza gráfica)

## Reglas de diseño para pantallas
1. SIEMPRE dark mode — fondo #000000 o #121212
2. El amarillo flúor #E1FF2D es SOLO para CTAs y highlights — no para fondos grandes
3. Máximo 2 colores corporativos dominantes por pantalla + flúor como acento
4. Textos siempre blancos sobre fondo oscuro, nunca grises claros
5. Iconografía: outlined, stroke 1.5-2px, estilo minimal
6. Espaciado generoso (16-24px entre secciones)
7. Cards: bordes redondeados 8px, sin sombra, borde sutil
8. Las imágenes de personajes se usan en onboarding y marketing, NO en UI funcional
9. Los gradientes se usan como fondo de headers/hero, NO en componentes interactivos

# SpecBox Control Panel — Design Guidelines

## Brand Identity
- Product: SpecBox Control Panel — internal observability & dev-team management tool over a Postgres Native Backend.
- Aesthetic: Custom, Linear-style (references: Linear, Vercel Dashboard, GitHub Projects, Datadog).
- Visual tone: technical, calm, precise. A daily-use power-user tool, NOT a marketing site.
- Default appearance: LIGHT. (A dark theme exists in code via a toggle; always generate LIGHT here.)

## Color System
- Primary: #0080FF (electric-blue) — CTAs, links, focus rings, active nav item, active claims.
- Secondary: #00B4D8 (cyan-tech) — secondary buttons, tags, the 'done' state.
- Tertiary/Accent: #7C3AED (violet) — highlights, notifications, progress emphasis.
- Neutral seed: #94A3B8 (slate) — borders, dividers, secondary text, disabled.
- Surfaces (light): page bg #F8FAFC (snow), cards #FFFFFF, alt sections #F1F5F9.
- Semantic: Success #10B981, Warning #F59E0B, Error #EF4444, Info #0080FF.
- RULE: Primary buttons = solid #0080FF bg, white text. Secondary buttons = white bg, 1px slate border.
- RULE: Card bg #FFFFFF on a #F8FAFC page. Never use gradients on backgrounds — flat colors only.

## UC Status colors (status semaphore, used sparingly)
- backlog: neutral grey badge (#F1F5F9 bg, #475569 text).
- in_progress: electric-blue badge (#E6F2FF bg, #004C99 text).
- review: amber badge (#FFFBEB bg, #92400E text).
- done: cyan badge (#E0F7FC bg, #006C82 text).

## Typography
- Headings: Sora, semibold/bold, sizes 30/24/20/18px (h1/h2/h3/h4). Page titles are contained (~30px) — this is a tool, not a hero.
- Body: Inter, regular, 16px base, line-height 1.5.
- Labels/captions/buttons: Inter, medium, 14px.
- Monospace (branch names, IDs, code): JetBrains Mono, 13px.
- RULE: max 2 font weights per card.

## Shape & Spacing
- Border radius: 8px base. Buttons 8px, cards 12px, inputs 8px, badges full/pill.
- Spacing: 4px grid. Card padding 16-20px. Section gaps 32px.
- RULE: all interactive elements >= 44px tap target on mobile.

## Layout — Linear-style shell
- Persistent LEFT SIDEBAR, 240px wide, collapsible to a 64px icon rail. Sidebar holds: brand wordmark (◆ SpecBox) + project switcher at top; nav items (Dashboard, Proyectos, Claims, Actividad, Equipo); theme toggle + user at bottom.
- TOP BAR inside the content area: breadcrumb (Proyecto › US-XXX › UC-YYY) on the left, a Cmd+K search trigger and actions on the right. 56-64px tall.
- MAIN content area uses the full width (no narrow centered column) to favor information density.
- A right-side DETAIL PANEL slides in when a table row (e.g. a UC) is selected.

## Component patterns
- Cards: #FFFFFF bg, 12px radius, shadow-sm, 1px border #E2E8F0, 16-20px padding.
- Metric tiles: large number (Sora) + label + small trend arrow + tiny sparkline.
- Data tables: dense, ~38px rows, sticky header with solid bg, left-aligned text, right-aligned numbers, status badge centered. Hover highlights the row. Keyboard navigable.
- Activity feed: vertical timeline, each item = colored dot + actor avatar + action text + relative time.
- Claims: a persistent badge 'avatar @ branch · 23h' using JetBrains Mono for the branch; a dedicated Claims table has a 'duration' column and a 'release' action; stale claims tinted with warning.
- Avatars: initials on a colored circle (rotating electric-blue / cyan / violet by developer).
- Buttons: 8px radius, 14px Inter medium, 12px 24px padding.
- Inputs: 8px radius, 1px #CBD5E1 border, focus ring 2px #0080FF/20%.
- Command palette (Cmd+K): centered overlay modal, search input + grouped results (projects / UCs / developers / actions).
- Empty states: minimal line illustration + one-line explanation + a primary action.
- Skeleton loaders (not spinners) that mirror the final layout.

## Motion (moderate, <200ms, 'calmer interface')
- page enter: fade + 8px slide-up, 180ms ease-out.
- row/button hover: subtle bg change, 120ms.
- panel/modal: scale 0.98->1 + fade, 140ms.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

## Responsive
- Desktop >=1024px: full shell (sidebar 240px + detail panel).
- Tablet 768-1023px: sidebar collapsed to icon rail; detail panel becomes an overlay.
- Mobile <768px: sidebar -> hamburger drawer + a bottom nav of 4 destinations (Dashboard, Proyectos, Claims, Equipo). Dense tables reflow to stacked cards (label:value), surfacing the 2-3 key fields.

## Do NOT
- Do NOT use gradients on backgrounds.
- Do NOT use a top horizontal nav as the primary navigation — the sidebar is primary.
- Do NOT center content in a narrow column — use width for density.
- Do NOT use spinners where a skeleton fits.
- Do NOT exceed shadow-md on cards.
- Do NOT mix sharp and rounded corners in the same view.
